Long ago — perhaps thousands of years ago, perhaps longer —
Two peoples rose upon this land at once.
One of them were called villagers.
Plain, conservative, they farmed, traded, and raised children, generation on generation.
Iron golems watched at night, bell towers told the hours, hearth-smoke rose between homes.
The other were called the ancient Builders.
They looked much as you do, but cleverer, hungrier to explore, wilder of heart.
They raised temples, carved the rock walls, studied the secrets of redstone.
At first, villagers and Builders kept to their own.
Now and then they traded — villagers gave bread, Builders gave redstone contraptions.
Both sides were content with that.
